correctness.rationale: In the surviving bipartite graph the only vertices that can exceed selected degree n-1 are intact vertices, and then only by their full n-edge stars. A surviving edge in the bounding fault rectangle is in no such star, so it is a cone point. If the rectangle is full and proper, the intact stars cover the ground set E of surviving edges, and selecting one edge from each intact star into a faulted vertex of the other class gives distinct private representatives. Put Q equal to E minus those chosen representatives. For each q in Q at any stage, a forbidden set containing q loses its constraint on deletion, and its private representative is a cone point there. Link formation replaces every forbidden set by that set minus q, leaving its private representative in place and still covering the remaining Q. Both star and deletion are contractible, so the gluing gives a suspension; at the last vertex the link consists only of the empty face and there are two contractible components. Here |Q|>=1 since there is an intact star of size n>=2 and exactly one chosen representative belongs to it. This yields S^(|E|-t-1), t=2n-|R|-|C|, and both displayed dimension forms follow. evidence: For a forbidden star S_i choose its private vertex p and put A=S_i minus {p}. Let H' have ground set E minus S_i and hyperedges S_j minus S_i for j unequal to i. The only edge incident to p is S_i, so the union in Kim's Theorem 1.2 is the single star st(A). A face in st(A) omits p; its part outside S_i must be in I(H'), and its part in A is arbitrary. Intersecting with st(p) excludes the full subset A and adds no other constraint, since p is private. Thus the actual intersection in the prior theorem is exactly the join of the boundary simplex on A with I(H'). Kim gives a suspension by |S_i|-1 dimensions for nonempty A; singleton S_i is a forbidden singleton and can simply be removed. H' again has all remaining private vertices and covers its ground set. Iterate, with the final single forbidden set giving a simplex boundary; if an intersection has empty realization the two nonempty stars are disjoint and give S^0. The summed suspension contributions give S^(|E|-t-1).

The Alexander dual is the union of simplices on E minus each intact star. Its nerve is the boundary of a simplex because every proper subfamily leaves a private edge uncovered while the entire family covers. Alexander duality alone in this route computes the specified integral homology, not the homotopy equivalence.

originality.rationale: The exact indexed graph formulation appeared only as the frozen record itself, and the closest graph-specific results are different. But the operative spherical-case lemma is a direct corollary of the prior hypergraph star-cluster theorem (Jinha Kim, arXiv:2408.14321v2, Theorem 1.2). Specialization at a private vertex gives the full suspension count, not merely a one-step existence statement. The remaining reduction to that lemma and to the isolated-vertex cone criterion is the immediate intact-star description. This is mathematical coverage by a stronger result, not a rejection based on scope similarity, access failure or catalogue nonreturn.
residual_risks: No assertion is made that the exact rectangular formula has previously been printed verbatim, or that the closest graph-specific same-day finding has priority.
Dong's unretrieved full text and other combinatorial-topology literature could provide additional coverage; the decisive coverage here does not depend on those sources.

value.rationale: As a mathematical classification, the partition into cones and homotopy spheres for all nonempty proper deletions is useful: equal-size faults can have opposite outcomes, and the dimension depends explicitly on two geometric fault extents. This gives a natural diagnostic for instability of the intact topology. That utility does not make the covered specialization an original finding.
